blocks.content: Andhra Pradesh has a rich and ancient cultural heritage that encompasses classical dance forms, music, literature, cuisine, festivals, and traditional arts and crafts.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Kuchipudi is the official classical dance form of Andhra Pradesh, originating from the Krishna district.
Telugu literature experienced its Golden Age under Emperor Sri Krishnadevaraya and the Ashta Diggajas during the Vijayanagara Empire.
Ugadi (Telugu New Year) and Makara Sankranti are the main cultural festivals celebrated across the state.
Traditional craft heritage includes GI-tagged arts like Kalamkari art, Kondapalli toys, and Etikoppaka lacquerware.
Andhra cuisine is celebrated for its distinctive spiciness, extensive use of Gongura (sorrel leaves), and rich culinary tradition.

blocks.content: Andhra Pradesh is renowned for Carnatic music, the classical music of South India. The state has produced legendary composers and musicians. The most famous is Tyagaraja (1767–1847), born in Tiruvarur (Tamil Nadu) but whose style was adopted by Andhra musicians; however, the Thyagaraja Aradhana is famously celebrated at Tiruvayaru (Tamil Nadu), bordering Andhra influence areas.

Syama Sastri (1762–1827) and Muthuswami Dikshitar (1775–1835), along with Tyagaraja, form the Trinity of Carnatic music. Pithapuram-born Semmangudi Srinivasa Iyer and Dwaram Venkataswamy Naidu (violin maestro from Vizianagaram) are legendary figures from Andhra Pradesh.

Telugu is known as the 'Italian of the East' for its melodious quality (attributed to the observation that it ends in vowel sounds). It is one of the classical languages of India, receiving the Classical Language status in 2008.

blocks.content: Andhra Pradesh cuisine is famous for its spicy and flavorful dishes, heavily influenced by the use of red and green chillies. It is considered among the spiciest regional cuisines in India.
